title: Multi-Tenant Database Architectures: Trade-Off Analysis at Scale
realWorldScenario: Your B2B SaaS startup is scaling from 100 to 10,000 enterprise customers, including Fortune 500 banks with strict data isolation and custom schema requirements. The VP of Engineering asks you to recommend the database architecture.
questionStatement: Conduct an exhaustive architectural trade-off analysis of the three multi-tenant PostgreSQL patterns: (1) Shared Database, Shared Schema with Row-Level Security; (2) Shared Database, Separate Schema per Tenant; and (3) Separate Database per Tenant. Evaluate each across system catalog limits, connection pool limits, migration complexity, and backup isolation.
expectedConcepts: Shared schema with RLS cost and migration simplicity
Database-per-tenant isolation, backup, and connection pooling cost
Noisy neighbor problem and noisy tenant partitioning
hints: What happens to pg_class when you have 10,000 schemas each with 100 tables?
How does single-tenant backup restore work in a shared schema?
Consider the hybrid approach used by companies like Salesforce and Slack.
